horses.spotlight_comment: Ran to a modest level in novices on good to soft ground last autumn (7f and 1m1f); upped in trip and tried in headgear for his reappearance and this 4,300,000gns yearling remains capable of better.

Sent off the odds-on favourite for his Southwell debut (1m3f) eight weeks ago and he ran on strongly to win by just shy of 3l; that form looks solid and he is open to plenty of improvement; looks a good prospect.

13,000euros yearling; ninth foal; half-brother to seven winners including Quian (1m-2m Flat including 2yo/German Group 3, RPR 104; 2m-2m3f hurdle) and Laggata (9.4f; 76); dam German 1m4f winner, half-sister to triple 1m4f Group 1 winner Quijano; should have a bright future but he makes his debut in a good novice.

Created a positive impression when easily winning a 1m4f novice at Southwell last month, coming home 3l clear of a stablemate of Pursuit Of Love; likely he will need more to follow up but he is still of serious interest.

Eighth foal; half-sister to six winners including Alkandora (10.5f Listed; RPR 107), Persian Royal (1m; 97) and Cambric (1m4f-1m6f; 84); dam Listed-placed 1m 2yo winner (103); one of two for William Haggas but Tom Marquand rides Chimes Of Thunder.

Dropped away in the final furlong on her Salisbury debut last October (7f, good; trained by David Menuisier), a race that developed into a three-furlong sprint; should appreciate today's longer trip and she's an interesting contender starting out for William Haggas (same owners).

Last September's Newmarket debut (7f, good to firm) was full of promise; failed to build on it when fifth of ten at Chelmsford last month but that run may have been needed and she can surely do better back on turf and upped in trip.
300-1 and finished well beaten on last month's Wolverhampton debut (8.6f).

425,000gns yearling; third foal; half-sister to winners Manara (1m-1m4f; RPR 89) and Dance Desire (Saudi Arabia 7f-1m1f); dam 6f winner (96), out of close relative of 1m2f Group 1 winner Wavering and half-sister to 1m2f 2yo Group 1 winner Mandaean; market strength would look significant.

horses.spotlight_comment: Second foal of a Group-placed 1m/1m2f winner (RPR 115), herself from a good family; makes her debut for a stable in good form and she needs a look in the betting.

Insole Jack Doughty 9-1 - - 82 Never in contention on her Wolverhampton debut in February (8.6f); fitted with a hood for her second start and she recorded a shock 50-1 success in a five-runner event over 1m at Southwell 23 days ago; this looks tougher under a penalty.

Smart pedigree; did really well to win a 1m fillies' novice at Chelmsford in December, blowing the start and having plenty to do turning for home but producing a fast finish to win under a hand ride; strong claims despite her penalty.

Won a valuable pot as a 2yo; slow to come to hand as a 3yo but he changed yards last summer and made an impressive winning return from a gelding operation last September (6f, good to soft; cheekpieces on for the first time); fine reappearance when third in the Listed Cammidge Trophy at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) four weeks ago; raised 3lb for his troubles and still has to prove his stamina for 7f.

Had strong handicap form over 1m in the second half of 2025, finishing second at York's Ebor meeting (good to firm) before recording back-to-back wins at Goodwood (good to soft and good); ran well for third in a Nottingham Listed race when last seen 178 days ago; only seventh in this race 12 months ago and he's 4lb higher today.

Began his career with two 7f AW wins and he was a fine second at Chester on his handicap debut last June (7f, good); fourth of 17 in a 1m handicap at Ascot when last seen nine months ago, a run that can be marked up as he raced away from the first three home; still has potential and he returns with his stable back in better form.

Paul Mulrennan 33-1 96 - - Progressive handicapper for the Crisfords and he was last seen finishing second in the Buckingham Palace at Royal Ascot (7f, good to firm) in June 2023; sold for 20,000gns in May 2024; only dropped 3lb during his 1038-day absence; likely best watched.

Came good at Goodwood last August (7f, good to firm), running on strongly to bag a Class 2 handicap; faced a stiff task in a Thirsk conditions event on his reappearance two weeks ago; opposable with his usual visor remaining absent.

horses.spotlight_comment: Strong handicap form over 7f last summer, winning at Goodwood and Chepstow as well as finishing second in a 20-runner event at Ascot (all when wearing blinkers); still feasibly weighted on that form and he went without headgear when down the field in the Lincoln; the blinkers return today and he's a leading contender.

Strong handicap form over 7f last summer, winning at Goodwood and Chepstow as well as finishing second in a 20-runner event at Ascot (all when wearing blinkers); still feasibly weighted on that form and he went without headgear when down the field in the Lincoln; the blinkers return today and he's a leading contender.

Finished second in a Group 1 in Australia in October 2024 (1m2f, good; visored first time); well short of his best in two runs in early 2025 and has since been gelded and transferred to Britain; had a wind op prior to this first start for Kevin Ryan; no easy task under top weight.

Began 2025 with 7f novice wins at Kempton and Doncaster; ended his 3yo campaign with a close third at Doncaster (7f, soft) 183 days ago; sold out of Roger Varian's stable for 85,000gns in October; still has low mileage, is yet to run a poor race when wearing a hood and is starting out for a trainer in great form; lots to like.

Well beaten at Doncaster on his return but he wasn't well drawn and has a modest record fresh; stepping up to 7f will give him more time to claw back the ground he's likely to forfeit at the start; on a dangerous mark and he's a lively outsider, for all his losing run stretches back to October 2023.

Close third in Listed company at Wolverhampton last month on his first attempt at 7f and he wasn't beaten for a lack of stamina; not at his best in a hot sprint handicap at Newcastle on Good Friday; no surprise to see him bounce back with a big run.

His latest Newcastle defeat isn't the run to judge him on and he had been progressing well beforehand; no problem with the return to turf and stepping back up to 7f will be of benefit; interesting with cheekpieces now given a go.
The winner of two of his six starts in France, both over 7f on ground slower than good; sold for 36,000euros in February; makes his stable debut in a competitive race.

horses.spotlight_comment: Shaped okay at Wolverhampton on her return from 11 months off in December but she failed to back it up at Southwell last month; dropping down the weights and this return to turf could be beneficial.

Two wins over shorter as a 3yo; improved when second at Kempton on his seasonal return last month (1m) and when third at Nottingham 17 days ago he found himself poorly positioned; well worth another crack at this trip and he should make a bold bid.
Three wins, two on soft ground, as a 3yo and he is now 9lb lower than for the latest; generally struggled last year though, before and after wind surgery, and he has too much to prove for comfort.
Back to winning ways with a front-running 10.3f success in the mud at Chester last September; this course winner will need to return at the top of his game if he is to defy this 4lb higher mark.
Scudamore Pierre-Louis Jamin 14-1 71 89 94 Four wins in 2025, including at this track (extended 1m3f); all of those were in cheekpieces (absent today) and others may have her measure.

His two peak efforts for Paddy Twomey came over 1m on soft ground; 50-1 when tailed off in the Spring Mile at Doncaster on his seasonal return; some encouragement for the longer trip on pedigree but he is not a solid option.

Three-time winner in France, the latest a claiming success over 1m4f at Longchamp last September (very soft ground); now tackles a much faster surface than he is accustomed to but his brother Ring Of Beara handled good, and probably good to firm too; betting to guide.

horses.spotlight_comment: On a fair mark on her best Flat form for Harry Charlton; some promise over hurdles for new stable and 1m4f may have stretched her when back on the Flat at Thirsk two weeks ago.

Ready winner of a 1m novice at Newcastle in January on his second outing; flopped when odds-on at Wolverhampton last month but was reported to have an irregular heartbeat afterwards; moves back up in trip for his handicap debut and he remains capable of better.

Only four ran when she won her novice at Newcastle (1m2f) last September; better form in handicaps on her last two starts, second at Newcastle (1m4f) and a close sixth in a Class 2 at Lingfield when last seen in December; still has time to better now returned to turf.

Ran up against smart types on first two 7f starts, on this track and at York (both on good), keeping on pleasingly into third on debut, then ran to similar level next time; was in the right place at the right time, unlike the second, when winning a C&D novice in September; open to improvement as a 3yo; goes handicapping with cheekpieces fitted.

Ten 2yo runs, winning three handicaps at about 1m (good to firm, good and soft); took a hefty rise for the latest of them and is now 12lb higher; creditable comeback at Musselburgh recently but surprising if she's well enough treated to win today; yard also runs Strength Of Spirit.

Bred to stay further than 1m but was sharp enough to win 6f Newbury novice (good to firm) on debut; found wanting in two later runs but in Listed company first and soft ground may not have suited back at Newbury (1m); gelded since; this first handicap looks competitive.

Golden pedigree, dam had four Group 1 winners (at 1m up to 2m4f) among her siblings, including Friendly Soul for this yard; this one hasn't been as dynamic as the latter so far and his defeat of some newcomers and handicap prospects on Kempton AW (1m; made all) 17 days ago was hard to assess in merit terms; needs more now handicapping but that's quite possible.

Maiden who ran well in all three handicaps at 7f and 1m, making most when runner-up over this trip at Newmarket (good) in September; this looks a tough race in which to get off the mark; yard also runs Mr Seagull.

Bright start, winning at Pontefract (6f, good to firm) then had work cut out trying to give weight to a promising newcomer on AW; big prices and well beaten in two sales races when last seen in September; gelded since and now goes in cheekpieces on handicap debut; faces a tough return upped to 1m.

Hit the front in the nick of time when justifying support on his Kempton AW debut in September but he was easily outpointed by a promising type on Southwell reappearance (1m) last month, when much more use was made of him; interesting to see the tactics on turf debut but should do better.

Needed every yard of 7f on Ayr debut (good) in August but the further she went the better she looked; the step up to 1m should have suited on Kempton AW in October but she found disappointingly little; returns to action with something to prove.

Has taken great strides since winning a seller last June, winning with authority on handicap debut at Newbury (7f, good to firm) on final 2yo start and he again had reserves when successful at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) this month; up 4lb but he's anything but exposed; respected.

Eight of her nine runs have come in novice/maiden company but her one handicap run saw her finish second over C&D last July off an 8lb higher mark; returns from an 86-day break without any accessories; betting useful.

horses.spotlight_comment: Followed August's 6f win at Nottingham with two solid efforts over 7f; down the field on this month's return to action at Kempton but that should have sharpened him up and he is feasibly weighted.
Early promise for James Horton last season but his campaign rather fizzled out; starts out for a new trainer (sold for 5,000gns in October) off a reduced mark; worth a market check.
Ended his 2yo campaign with a couple of creditable runs in 7f AW nurseries; drops back to 6f for his seasonal return and with blinkers enlisted (wore cheekpieces final 2yo run); others look stronger.

Insole Jack Doughty 9-2 69 57 74 6f AW winner in November (form solid) and several good placed runs followed; he has more to prove on turf but he won't be far away if able to transfer his form back to the grass.
More encouraging signs with his staying-on fourth of 13 at Newcastle (6f) 12 days ago; dropped 2lb for his troubles and now has headgear added for the first time; could have a bigger effort lurking.

Two promising 5f runs to begin his career (trained by Adrian Keatley as a 2yo) but he didn't get home over 6f when last seen; gelded and sporting a hood on this seasonal/stable/handicap debut; opening mark not an obvious gift though.
Failed to win in five 2yo runs but has shown ability on both AW and turf; this is a deeper race than he was contesting when last seen though.
Six-race maiden but she went close at Bath (5f, good) three weeks ago on her return from a six-month absence; returning to 6f should be fine and she is not fully exposed just yet; major contender.

Second of seven on his nursery debut last July (7f, good to firm) but that was followed by two lacklustre efforts (gelded before latest); back down in trip for his reappearance and goes in blinkers for the first time.
6f maiden win at Wolverhampton in November; better form when second of 12 in a 6f handicap at Southwell 18 days ago; 1lb higher today but still a key player if able to transfer AW form back to turf.

No immediate improvement for the switch to handicaps when eighth of nine over 7f here seven months ago; his novice and maiden runs had threatened better though and he still has time to fulfil that promise; betting useful.
No threat when sixth of seven on her handicap debut at Lingfield (6f, AW) 31 days ago; dropped 3lb and now tried in cheekpieces but others bring stronger claims.

Prominent racer; close second at Newcastle (6f) last month but he failed to back it up at Southwell three weeks ago; all his best efforts have come on a straight course so perhaps can be given the benefit of the doubt for last time; one of two runners for the stable; not discounted.

horses.spotlight_comment: Promising return to action at Chelmsford in October (6f) and that was off a 6lb higher mark; no progress since but 7f has stretched him on his last two starts and he returns to 6f in a lower grade; big player with cheekpieces added for the first time.
Conditions shouldn't be an excuse and he didn't run badly at Bath (5f, good) three weeks ago after a short break; Tom Marquand a notable booking; each-way shout.

No win on turf since September 2024 but he ran well for third at Thirsk (6f, good) two weeks ago, form that has been boosted by the winner and second running well in big fields since; one to be interested in off the same mark.

The winner of two of his six starts this year, both over 6f at Southwell; he could only manage fourth of the nine runners back at Southwell 20 days ago and he will need to raise his game to defy this mark.

No better than midfield in three sprint novice runs in the latter part of 2025 and his opening mark looks tough on that evidence; looks the type his trainer will do well with now handicapping though and a much more prominent showing could be on the cards.

Paul Mulrennan 12-1 69 62 79 Won a 6f novice at Newcastle on his second start last summer; handicaps have proved more troublesome but he is edging down the weights and now drops into 0-70 company for the first time.

Sprung a surprise in a soft-ground 6f maiden at Windsor last September; 50-1 and well beaten in two handicaps since (1m and 7f, both Polytrack); return to 6f and the addition of cheekpieces may turn things around but it is still easy to have reservations.
Knocking at the door over 6f and 7f on AW this year; won't mind getting back on turf and he should give it another good go from the front.

It took a drop into classified company for him to return to winning ways in February (6f, AW; blinkered first time; final run for John Butler); gained a second Newcastle win of the year last month but he raced far too freely back there on Monday; up in class today and likely vulnerable.

Strong at the finish when winning a 7f handicap at Doncaster last summer (good to soft); three lesser efforts followed and he returns from his 172 break over a trip that may be too sharp; he is drawn near some good pace though and looks worth a market check.
